title: Ear pain after swimming

doorway: My left ear hurts and feels blocked.

Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.
Use the time limit stated for your selected practice mode.

patient.name: Jordan Park
patient.persona: I am a lifeguard and wear earbuds during my commute. I live with my brother.
patient.opening: My left ear hurts and feels blocked.

opening_contract.text: My left ear hurts and feels blocked.

patient.affect: I want to know what is causing this and how to get back to my usual activities.

education_responses.student: The ear examination will guide treatment. If canal infection is confirmed, drops and keeping the ear dry usually help. We will avoid neomycin because of your reaction. Come back if it is not improving within two to three days.
education_responses.patient: Thank you. I understand that the next steps depend on the examination and tests.

education_responses.student: We can discuss temporary dry duties at the pool so the ear can recover without unnecessary time off.

model_note.S:
CC: My left ear hurts and feels blocked.

HPI: 24-year-old male. Left otalgia for 2 days. Pain at left canal opening. Aching and pruritus. Pain 5/10. Persistent daily discomfort. Pruritus preceded pain and muffled hearing. Recent swimming and new in-ear earbuds. Pain with ear contact/earbud insertion; mild chewing-related jaw ache. Partial relief without earbud. Acetaminophen 500 mg once; no ear drops. Prior earbud-related itching, no prior otalgia.

PMH: No chronic illness; nocturnal bruxism.

PSH: No ear surgery, tympanostomy or known perforation.

Meds: No regular medication.

SH: Never smoked or vaped. One or two beers weekly. No recreational drugs. Lifeguard; earbud use during commute. Lives with brother.

FH: Father: hearing loss requiring aids in his 60s. Mother: hypertension; brother: no known major illness.

Allergies: Neomycin: pruritic erythematous skin reaction.

ROS: Heent: Muffled left hearing. Small clear left ear discharge. No sore throat. General: No fever. No chills. No systemic malaise. Neurologic: No vertigo. No headache. No facial weakness.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 118/74 mmHg, P 72 bpm, R 14 rpm, T 98.4 F oral, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 10", Wt 166 lbs

General: Alert, well appearing.
HEENT: Left tragal/pinna manipulation tender; canal erythematous and edematous with scant debris. Left tympanic membrane visualized and intact without bulging. Right canal without erythema or edema; right membrane intact and nonbulging; no mastoid tenderness. No enlarged or tender cervical nodes. Oropharynx without erythema or exudate.
Musculoskeletal: Mild left temporomandibular joint tenderness with jaw opening; no facial swelling.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Osteopathic: C2 left paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 2. Allergic contact dermatitis of the ear canal
3. Temporomandibular disorder with referred ear pain
P: 1. Treat with appropriate topical otic therapy and analgesia after membrane review; avoid neomycin given the skin reaction. Teach drop administration and keep the ear dry, avoiding earbuds and swabs. Reassess if not improving within 48–72 hours. Fever, spreading swelling, severe worsening pain or new facial weakness needs prompt evaluation.

2. Remove the new earbud exposure and avoid unnecessary topical sensitizers. If dermatitis persists after infection treatment, consider ENT/dermatology assessment and guided topical anti-inflammatory treatment; explain that contact allergy is not confirmed by itching alone.

3. Reduce gum chewing and clenching; discuss gentle jaw care and dental assessment for persistent symptoms. Use safe analgesia if needed and explain that jaw treatment does not replace treatment of the inflamed canal.
